transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-30 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~1:02 | Recording: yes
Attendees (as calendar): Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Nexalytics Head of Platform), Luis Herrera (Nexalytics Sr ML Eng), Sarah Kim (Finance), Owen Park (DevOps)

Summary:
Year-end health check focusing on usage spikes in November, cost variances across embeddings vs gen, reliability incidents (3 minor), and roadmap handoff for Q1 pilots (quantization, autoscale tuning, dedicated capacity increase). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send detailed cost CSV and run a dedicated stability benchmark; Nexalytics to confirm procurement timeline.

Topics:
- Last quarter usage & cost drivers
- Incident review: 2026-11-18 & 2026-12-03 outages and mitigations
- Dedicated vs Hosted sizing for Q1 pilot
- Security/compliance items (SOC2 scope, SSO/SAML, KMS)
- Roadmap: quantization pilot, autoscale policy updates, KV cache tuning

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, auto transcript; some words may be slightly off)
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone thanks for joining, happy holidays, we'll run 60ish minutes. Quick intro - I'm Jordan AE, Priya is our SE, Ethan's the CSM. Maya over to you for a quick context setting?
[00:14] Maya Patel: Sure, thanks. Hi all, Nexalytics is running Redwood Hosted for the user-facing chat flows and Dedicated pools for heavy batch embed jobs. We're seeing cost creep on embeddings and a couple of latency spikes that affect nightly pipelines. We want to close the year with a clear pilot scope for Q1.
[00:28] Luis Herrera: to add, our embed jobs spiked in Nov after the search roll out and we didn't fully understand tokenization differences, so some calls are longer than we expected.
[00:39] Priya Desai: got it. we'll pull the token distribution but preliminarily that sounds like a combination of prompt framing and some clients sending full HTML. We can prefix-strip and push smaller context. Also want to note we saw KV cache misses on some sessions which upped cost. (small chuckle) the transcriber may record K-V cash, apologies.
[00:57] Sarah Kim: from finance side, we moved budget this month but need a clean view of per-route cost; the bill looks higher because of embeddings volume and a couple of high-latency retries. Was there a retry storm on Nov 18?
[01:12] Ethan Cole: yes we flagged Nov 18, there was a networking hiccup that caused retries on the Dedicated pool; Redwood applied a fallback to hosted for a subset which kept user facing flows up but increased token counts. We have notes in the incident playbook link — will share.
[01:30] Maya Patel: ok on the incident — can we get a root cause write up in the ticket with mitigation steps?
[01:36] Jordan Reyes: absolutely, we'll push the RCA and the trace links; Priya will attach latency traces and cpu/gpu utilization.
[01:42] Priya Desai: quick clarification: when we talk Dedicated pool we mean the reserved GPU capacity (you had v2 nodes), is that right Owen?
[01:49] Owen Park: yes we've got a 4xV100 equivalent setup, but some jobs landed on a mixed fleet last month during autoscale which changed perf.
[02:00] Priya Desai: that explains variance — mixed fleet can cause kernel selection diffs. we'll include a recommended node profile to avoid interop.
[02:12] (crosstalk)
[02:20] Jordan Reyes: moving to costs — Jordan: Sarah do you have permission to share a finance summary?
[02:25] Sarah Kim: I can share. Our ask: tokenized bill for Nov-Dec, broken down by route (chat/gen vs embeddings vs rerank) and anomaly rows for retries and fallbacks. We also need estimated Q1 run-rate if pilot scales to 2x current embeddings.
[02:39] Jordan Reyes: note taken. we'll provide a CSV and a pivoted sheet. I'm also going to add a modeled run-rate with quantization 4-bit and batching optimizations so you can see upside.
[02:50] Luis Herrera: about quantization — we attempted a local 8-bit but saw a quality drop for longer prompts. Is Redwood's quant recommendation tuned by sequence len?
03:02 Priya Desai: yes, we profile across seq lengths. our Optimize tool suggests 4-bit with per-layer calibration for gen-heavy routes, but embeddings sometimes degrade on some open models; we'll run a small A/B on your embed model.
[03:20] Maya Patel: can you run a POC with our embed model and a 1M example subset? That would be helpful.
[03:26] Priya Desai: absolutely. we'll need a sanitized sample — please confirm data residency requirements (which region) and whether we should use tokenized hashes.
[03:36] Maya Patel: US-only, SOC2 scope applies and we must use token hashes, not raw text. Will send contact for compliance.
[03:44] Jordan Reyes: thanks. next: reliability incidents — Ethan, quick recap of the Dec 3 incident?
[03:50] Ethan Cole: Dec 3 saw a slow ramp where one of your autoscale triggers under-provisioned because of a misconfigured aggregate metric - essentially the scale up didn't fire until latency breached SLA. That caused queued requests and some timeouts; we rolled to hosted fallback for low tier traffic. We recommend adjusting the autoscale policy thresholds and using request-rate as an early signal.
[04:12] Owen Park: curious — what's the cost delta when fallback to hosted occurs? because last time fallback reduced latency but cost spiked.
[04:20] Jordan Reyes: it depends on workload; in your case the model variants differ: hosted used a cheaper open model but token counts rose due to retries. we estimate a 25-40% cost premium during those 3 hours. we'll show exact figures.
[04:35] Sarah Kim: that's material. we need guardrails to prevent fallback being more expensive than degraded latency. can Redwood set cost-aware fallback policies?
[04:45] Priya Desai: yes — routing policies can be cost-aware. you can set a budget override: if expected cost exceeds X, it prefers a cheaper model variant or queue with graceful degrade. we'll show config examples.
[04:59] Luis Herrera: technical deep dive — on autoscale, are we using request-based or token-based scaling? currently we use CPU% which is noisy.
[05:10] Priya Desai: request-rate is better for short gen flows; token-based can be useful for large batch embed jobs. we can help craft separate policies for your chat vs batch pipelines.
[05:25] Jordan Reyes: moving onto the Q1 roadmap — proposed pilots: 1) quantization A/B on embeddings 2) Dedicated pool sizing increase + node profile lock 3) autoscale policy rewrite and KV cache tuning 4) cost-monitoring alerts. Thoughts?
[05:40] Maya Patel: sounds right; prioritized 1 and 3. quantization gives immediate cost wins, autoscale reduces incidents. Dedicated sizing is contingent on procurement approval.
[05:49] Sarah Kim: procurement timeline — we need cost predictability to sign commit by Jan 12. If Redwood can show modeled run-rate with and without quantization that would help.
[05:59] Jordan Reyes: we'll do that.
[06:05] (longer discussion where Priya explains benchmarking plan)
[06:18] Priya Desai: Plan for the benchmark: we'll spin up a dedicated test pool with the same node profile, run mixed workloads (50% embeds, 50% gen) across seq lengths 128/512/1024. We'll capture p50/p95 latencies, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and retry counts. We'll run two runs: baseline and quantized. Each run ~24 hours to capture diurnal effects.
[06:42] Luis Herrera: 24 hours seems long — can we do a 48-hour one to catch weekend behavior?
[06:48] Priya Desai: yes ok 48 hours if you want — we suggested 24 for cost but 48 gives more confidence. We'll do 48 as requested.
[06:56] Jordan Reyes: Priya will share the benchmark script and the runbook.
[07:02] (discussion about security)
[07:10] Maya Patel: on compliance, SOC2 scope — we need to confirm retention of logs and if Redwood supports bring-your-own-KMS. Also SSO is mandatory.
[07:20] Priya Desai: we support BYOK via KMS integration and can limit log retention windows per route; SSO via SAML is available. We'll attach the security pack. Note: the transcript may show K-M-S as KMS or K-M-S; please ignore.
[07:31] Jordan Reyes: we'll share the security whitepaper and the SOC2 report stub.
[07:36] Sarah Kim: also, audit logs — we need per-request traceability for three months. Can Redwood provide that volume estimate?
[07:45] Ethan Cole: yes we can estimate. audit logs will add to storage costs; we'll produce an estimate in the cost CSV.
[07:53] (mid-call clarification and a minor transcription glitch)
[08:05] Owen Park: small note — our infra team prefers region-specific fallbacks (us-east only) to avoid cross-region egress.
[08:13] Priya Desai: fine — we can set region-first routing. We'll include those settings in the runbook.
[08:20] (discussion shifts to SLOs and KPIs)
[08:28] Jordan Reyes: proposed SLOs: p95 < 500ms for chat gen, p95 < 800ms for embeddings; availability 99.9 for dedicated pool. Acceptable?
[08:39] Maya Patel: p95 < 500ms for chat is tight but ok as a target. We'll run the bench to validate.
[08:45] Luis Herrera: for embeddings p95 800ms seems fine.
[08:49] Jordan Reyes: okay.
[09:00] (longer section where Priya reads out current numbers)
[09:05] Priya Desai: current observed: chat p95 630ms, chat p50 180ms; embed p95 1.2s. KV cache hit ratio ~72% on peak. Retry rate spiked to 4.3% during Nov 18.
[09:26] Sarah Kim: if retry rate drops to <1% what's the expected cost decrease?
[09:30] Jordan Reyes: ballpark 8-12% depending on where retries occurred; we'll show scenarios.
[09:36] (discussion about tooling)
[09:40] Ethan Cole: we'll set up route-level dashboards in the Redwood Console and add token-level breakdowns. We'll also add alerting for retry-rate > 1% and cost burn > $X/day.
[09:52] Maya Patel: can we grant our finance team view-only to console?
[09:55] Jordan Reyes: yes role-based access (RBAC) can give view-only to Sarah. We'll include instructions for SSO provision.
[10:02] (pause - people grab notes)
[10:22] Luis Herrera: two technical asks: 1) can Redwood share the exact kernel versions used in the dedicated pool (for reproducibility) 2) can we pin models per route?
[10:32] Priya Desai: yes and yes; we can export kernel/cuda/python stack and you can pin model version per route with rollouts. Pinning prevents unexpected rollouts.
[10:40] (discussion on model variants and fallbacks)
[10:48] Jordan Reyes: on fallbacks we recommend a fallback chain: same model version in hosted region, then cheaper model variant if cost threshold exceeded, then degraded response with a polite note.
[10:59] Maya Patel: ok acceptable.
[11:05] (wrap up - recap and next steps)
[11:10] Jordan Reyes: quick recap: Redwood to send cost CSV + modeled run-rate with quantization by Jan 4; Priya to run 48-hour benchmark on dedicated profile and share results Jan 7; Ethan to calendar pilot kickoff and attach pre-read; Nexalytics to send compliance contact and hashed sample data. Any objections?
[11:26] Sarah Kim: none. Thanks.
[11:30] Maya Patel: thanks folks, appreciate the thoroughness. We'll sync after the benchmark. Happy holidays.
[11:36] Jordan Reyes: thanks everyone. End recording.
